title: COP31 Climate Talks Face Crisis as Fossil Fuel Mentions Removed
subtitle: Global leaders struggle to reach an agreement as environmental groups warn of a 'ghost summit' with no real action.

summary.en: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey is currently in a state of crisis. Organizers have removed all mentions of fossil fuels from the latest draft agreement. This move has angered many countries and environmental campaigners who fear the event will fail to produce meaningful results. Panama has threatened to block the final outcome unless their demands are met. The summit is now facing pressure to restore stronger climate commitments before it ends.
summary.zh: 在土耳其舉行的第31屆聯合國氣候變遷大會目前陷入危機。主辦單位已從最新協議草案中刪除了所有關於化石燃料的提及。此舉激怒了許多國家與環保倡議人士，他們擔憂此次會議將無法產生具意義的成果。巴拿馬已威脅除非其要求獲得滿足，否則將阻擋最終結果。峰會目前面臨壓力，必須在結束前恢復更強硬的氣候承諾。

paragraphs.en: The COP31 climate summit in Turkey is facing a difficult moment as it enters its final hours. On Thursday, the event organizers released a new draft of the main agreement, but it contained a surprise change: every mention of fossil fuels had been removed. This decision has caused deep frustration among many participants, leading some to call the event a “ghost summit”—a meeting that exists in name but fails to produce any real, meaningful change.
paragraphs.zh: 在土耳其舉行的第31屆聯合國氣候變遷大會（COP31）進入最後倒數階段，正面臨艱難時刻。週四，主辦單位發布了主要協議的最新草案，但其中出現了一項令人驚訝的變動：所有關於化石燃料的提及皆被刪除。這項決定引起許多與會者的強烈不滿，甚至有人稱此次會議為「幽靈峰會」，意指這場會議僅有名義，卻無法產生任何實質且具意義的改變。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, the first version of the document was 18 pages long and included clear goals for moving away from fossil fuels. However, the new version is much shorter and has removed these important promises. The joint leaders of the summit, representing Australia and Turkey, also weakened goals related to electrification and failed to explain how wealthy nations will provide the money needed to help developing countries deal with the climate crisis. This financial support is essential for poorer nations to adapt to extreme weather and transition to cleaner energy sources.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，該文件的初版長達18頁，並包含明確的脫離化石燃料目標。然而，新版本篇幅大幅縮減，且刪除了這些重要的承諾。代表澳洲與土耳其的峰會共同主席，也削弱了與電氣化相關的目標，且未能說明富裕國家將如何提供資金，以協助開發中國家應對氣候危機。這筆財務支援對於較貧窮的國家適應極端天氣並轉型至更乾淨的能源來源至關重要。

paragraphs.en: This development has led to strong reactions from around the world. Panama, in an unusual move, sent a letter to the summit presidents stating that it would block any final agreement unless its demands for stronger action were met. Juan Carlos Navarro, the environment minister for Panama, noted that while the speeches at the summit have been beautiful, they do not match the reality of a planet that is being destroyed. He argued that the world expects radical change, but the current negotiations are not delivering it.
paragraphs.zh: 此一發展引發全球強烈反應。巴拿馬採取了罕見的行動，致函峰會主席，聲明除非其對採取更強硬行動的要求獲得滿足，否則將阻擋任何最終協議。巴拿馬環境部長納瓦洛（Juan Carlos Navarro）指出，雖然峰會上的演講內容動聽，但與地球正遭受破壞的現實並不相符。他主張，世界期待的是激進的變革，但目前的談判卻未能達成。

paragraphs.en: Many environmental campaigners agree with this assessment. Mohamed Adow, director of the Power Shift Africa thinktank, told The Guardian that the summit has been “muzzled,” or silenced, by countries that produce fossil fuels and do not want to commit to a transition away from them. He warned that if the current text remains as it is, the summit will have nothing to show for the time and effort spent in Turkey. Other groups, such as 350.org, have described the situation as an embarrassing lack of leadership. Andreas Sieber from 350.org stated that the leaders have turned one of the most important challenges of our time into an “inconvenient paragraph” that they would rather delete than address.
paragraphs.zh: 許多環保倡議人士認同此一評估。非洲能源轉型智庫（Power Shift Africa）主任阿多（Mohamed Adow）向《衛報》表示，峰會已遭到生產化石燃料且不願承諾轉型的國家「封口」。他警告，若目前的文本維持原樣，這場峰會將無法展現任何在土耳其投入的時間與心力所換來的成果。其他團體如「350.org」則形容此情況為令人尷尬的領導力匱乏。來自350.org的希伯（Andreas Sieber）表示，各國領袖已將當代最重要的挑戰之一，變成了他們寧可刪除也不願面對的「不便段落」。

paragraphs.en: Financial support remains a major point of disagreement. Rachitaa Gupta from the Global Campaign to Demand Climate Justice pointed out that the cause of the climate crisis is well-known, as is the question of who should pay for the damage. She criticized the “global north”—the wealthier, more developed nations—for their lack of political resolve. Many experts argue that it is unfair to expect developing countries to pay for a global transition to clean energy when they lack the necessary funds. They believe that the failure of rich countries to provide this money is a historic disgrace and a clear sign of a lack of political responsibility.
paragraphs.zh: 財務支援仍是主要的分歧點。「要求氣候正義全球運動」（Global Campaign to Demand Climate Justice）的古普塔（Rachitaa Gupta）指出，氣候危機的成因眾所皆知，誰該為損害買單的問題亦然。她批評「全球北方」（即較富裕、較發達的國家）缺乏政治決心。許多專家認為，在開發中國家缺乏必要資金的情況下，要求他們為全球能源轉型買單是不公平的。他們認為，富裕國家未能提供這筆資金是歷史性的恥辱，也是缺乏政治責任感的明確跡象。

paragraphs.en: Negotiations at COP summits require consensus, which means that every country must agree on the final text before it is accepted. Because of this rule, Panama’s decision to stand against the current draft has the potential to stop the entire process. If other nations choose to support Panama, the summit could end without a clear agreement on how to limit global temperature rises or protect the most vulnerable communities from the worst effects of climate change.
paragraphs.zh: COP峰會的談判需要達成共識，這意味著在協議被接受前，每個國家都必須同意最終文本。由於這項規則，巴拿馬決定反對當前草案的舉動，有可能會導致整個程序停擺。若其他國家選擇支持巴拿馬，峰會可能會在沒有達成如何限制全球升溫，或保護最脆弱群體免受氣候變遷最嚴重影響的明確協議下結束。

paragraphs.en: As the final hours of the summit approach, the pressure on the Australian and Turkish presidencies is increasing. They must now decide whether to listen to the demands of countries like Panama and environmental groups, or continue with a weakened agreement that many fear will be ignored by the rest of the world. For now, the future of the COP31 outcome remains uncertain, leaving the world to watch and wait to see if leaders can find a way to move past their disagreements and create a plan that truly addresses the climate crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著峰會進入最後幾小時，澳洲與土耳其主席團面臨的壓力與日俱增。他們現在必須決定，是要傾聽像巴拿馬這類國家與環保團體的訴求，還是要繼續推動一份被許多人擔憂將遭世界忽視的弱化協議。目前，COP31的結果仍充滿不確定性，全世界都在關注並等待，看領袖們是否能找到方法跨越分歧，制定出一份真正能解決氣候危機的計畫。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop or prevent something from happening or moving forward.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（街區、積木），這裡作動詞用。文中：Panama, in an unusual move, sent a letter to the summit presidents stating that it would block any final agreement unless its demands for stronger action were met.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To have a visible result or benefit after spending time or effort on something.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （花費時間或精力後）有具體的成果或收穫。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個片語，意指努力後卻沒有得到應有的回報。文中：He warned that if the current text remains as it is, the summit will have nothing to show for the time and effort spent in Turkey.
這裡的 stand 作動詞，與 against 搭配表示立場上的對抗。文中：Because of this rule, Panama’s decision to stand against the current draft has the potential to stop the entire process.

quiz.question: What specific change was made to the main agreement draft on Thursday?

options.A: The document was expanded to include more detailed financial plans.
options.B: All references to fossil fuels were removed from the text.
options.C: The summit duration was extended to allow for more negotiations.
options.D: The leadership of the summit was transferred from Australia and Turkey to Panama.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，週四發布的新草案中，所有關於「化石燃料」（fossil fuels）的提及都被刪除了。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到文件反而變短了；選項 C 文章未提及延長會議時間；選項 D 錯誤，因為澳洲與土耳其仍是共同領導者，只是面臨壓力。

quiz.question: Why does Panama's opposition have the potential to disrupt the entire summit process?

options.A: Panama is the largest financial contributor to the COP31 summit.
options.B: Panama has threatened to leave the UN if their demands are not met.
options.C: The summit rules require unanimous agreement from all participating countries.
options.D: Panama is leading a coalition of wealthy nations to block the agreement.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段，COP 會議的談判需要「共識」（consensus），這意味著所有國家必須同意最終文本才能通過。因此，巴拿馬的拒絕確實有權力阻止整個流程。選項 A、B 文章未提及；選項 D 錯誤，因為巴拿馬是為了要求更強力的氣候行動，而非代表富裕國家。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the author mean by saying the summit has been 'muzzled'?

options.A: The summit has been given more resources to succeed.
options.B: The summit's ability to take meaningful action has been restricted.
options.C: The summit has successfully silenced fossil fuel lobbyists.
options.D: The summit has become too loud and disorganized to function.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。原文中提到 summit 被 'muzzled'（被噤聲），隨後解釋是因為某些生產化石燃料的國家不願承諾轉型，導致會議無法做出實質決策。Muzzle 原意為「給動物戴口套」，在此隱喻會議被限制、無法自由發揮其應有的氣候治理功能。其他選項皆與語境不符。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of this article regarding the COP31 summit?

options.A: The summit has successfully united all nations toward a common climate goal.
options.B: The summit is a technical success despite minor disagreements between participants.
options.C: The summit is failing to address the climate crisis due to a lack of political courage and leadership.
options.D: The summit is primarily focused on the economic growth of developing nations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章整體基調在批評 COP31 刪除化石燃料相關承諾、缺乏財政支持以及領導力不足，導致會議面臨失敗風險。選項 A 與事實相反；選項 B 過於樂觀，與文章中「ghost summit」及「embarrassing lack of leadership」的描述衝突；選項 D 並非文章討論的核心議題。
